newsitem.title: USA: Man arrested in murder of comedian Bill Cosby's son.
newsitem.headline: Man arrested in murder of comedian Bill Cosby's son.

text.p: A man was arrested on Wednesday in connection with the murder of Ennis Cosby, the only son of comedian and actor Bill Cosby, police said.
Los Angeles police chief Willie Williams, in a late night press conference, declined to name the suspect, but said, "We are very comfortable ... that this is the man and he is the shooter."

Ennis Cosby, 27, was shot to death in the early hours of Jan. 16 while changing a flat tire near a freeway off-ramp in an exclusive suburb of Los Angeles in a murder that shocked the showbusiness community as well as the popular comedian's millions of fans.

Williams, in his brief statement to reporters, said the suspect was a white, adult male who lived in the San Fernando Valley area of Los Angeles and would probably be formally charged with Ennis Cosby's death on Thursday.

Cosby, a doctoral student at Columbia University in New York City, apparently pulled off the freeway to change a flat tire and police said at the time he was killed by his assailant with a single gunshot. They also said they suspected Cosby was killed in a bungled robbery attempt as nothing appeared to have been taken from his $130,000 Mercedes Benz car.

Williams said Bill Cosby, who starred in television's long-running "The Cosby Show," in which he played a doctor, and his wife Camille, had been informed of the arrest. Cosby described his son as "my hero" following his murder, referring to his overcoming a severe learning disability to succeed in college.

Williams said two other people, a man and a woman, had also been detained on Wednesday in connection with Ennis Cosby's murder and were being questioned by police. He said it had not been determined if they would be charged in the case.

The arrested suspect, Williams said, resembled a drawing made by a police artist from a description of the shooter given by a key witness in the case, a 47-year-old woman who was an acquaintance of the younger Cosby.

Police earlier said the woman was on her way to meet Ennis Cosby when he called her on his cellular phone to say he was stopping to change a flat tire. She told police that as she stopped by Cosby's car, a man tapped on her window and she drove off afraid, returning later to find Cosby shot to death.
Two weekly tabloid newspapers offered a combined $300,000 for information leading to the arrest of Ennis Cosby's killer or killers, and local authorities also offered rewards.
